title: FAR Module 5 · TBS 1

fields.label: 4. Remaining Donor-Restricted Amount After the Release

html:
TASK-BASED SIMULATION

Contribution Classification

Analyze contributions, donor restrictions, and releases from restriction.

Scenario

Hope Foundation reports the following transactions during the year.

Hope Foundation does not elect to report donor-restricted contributions whose restrictions are satisfied in the same period as contributions without donor restrictions.

  • Donor A contributes $90,000 with no donor-imposed restriction.
  • Donor B contributes $140,000 and requires that the money be used only for educational programs.
  • During the year, Hope Foundation spends $60,000 on qualifying educational costs that satisfy part of Donor B's restriction.

Required

1. Contribution Revenue Without Donor Restrictions
2. Contribution Revenue With Donor Restrictions
3. Release From Restriction
4. Remaining Donor-Restricted Amount After the Release
explanation:
Item 1 — Unrestricted Contribution

Contribution Revenue Without Donor Restrictions = $90,000

Item 2 — Donor-Restricted Contribution

Contribution Revenue With Donor Restrictions = $140,000

Item 3 — Release From Restriction

Hope Foundation used $60,000 for the exact educational purpose specified by the donor.

Release From Restriction = $60,000

Item 4 — Remaining Restricted Amount

Original Restricted Contribution $140,000 − Release $60,000 = $80,000 Remaining

CPA Takeaway

  • No donor restriction → net assets without donor restrictions.
  • Donor purpose restriction → net assets with donor restrictions.
  • Satisfying the restriction → release from restriction.
  • A release changes classification; it is not a second contribution.
